title: Civil-rights leadership comparison
goal: Students can distinguish shared leadership traits from each figure's distinct approaches.

rubric.must: Two named central figures are visible on opposite sides.
Shared traits appear in central bubbles connected to both figures.
Unique traits appear only on their respective outer sides.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the comparison/double-bubble exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The diagram faithfully compares both figures: three shared traits sit between the two central bubbles and connect to both; each figure’s two distinct approaches appear on that figure’s outer side. Labels are readable, and there are no material overlaps or cropping.

items.evidence: Martin Luther King Jr. is the left central bubble and Malcolm X is the right central bubble.
The central bubbles read “Civil-rights leadership,” “Powerful public speaking,” and “Sought Black dignity and equality”; each is connected to both figures.
The left side shows “Nonviolent direct action” and “Southern Christian Leadership Conference”; the right side shows “Black nationalism emphasis” and “Nation of Islam spokesperson.”
Visible connector lines link each shared bubble to both central figures and link each unique bubble to its respective figure.
All bubble labels are legible, with no material overlap or cropping.
